plan.notes: Term-by-term sequence transcribed verbatim from the official 2024-2025 American International College 'Program Plan' for Psychology (School of Business, Arts and Sciences). Semester totals printed on the plan: 15+16+16+15+16+14+15+15 = 122 credits (TOTAL CREDITS: 122). The program is a Bachelor of Arts (standard for AIC social science programs; the plan does not print a degree abbreviation). PSY2820/2821 Advanced Statistics and Lab is 4 credits (3+1); PSY3615 Experimental Psychology is 4 credits. The three 'PSYXXXX, Psychology Elective' slots (Sophomore Spring, Junior Fall, Junior Spring) are three additional psychology courses (9 credits) selected with the advisor. Major requirements: any Philosophy course (PHIXXXX, Gen Ed Category 4), PSY1200 Introduction to Psychology, PSY2302 Statistics, PSY2600 Foundations in Psychology, PSY2617 Cognitive Psychology, PSY2820 Advanced Statistics + PSY2821 Lab, PSY3422 Physiological Psychology, PSY3615 Experimental Psychology, plus PSY4865 Senior Seminar in Psychology and PSY4899 Psychology Practicum (one in Senior Fall, the other in Senior Spring — transcribed as printed). A practicum completed in another department with an acceptable psychological component may fulfill the practicum requirement; double majors need only one practicum. General Education categories per the 2024-2025 plan: Cat 1 Scientific World (math + science with lab; PSY2302 counts as the math), Cat 2 Self and Others (PSY1200 counts), Cat 3 Interdisciplinarity (ENG1202/ENG1602 + INT courses), Cat 4 Arts and Humanities, Cat 5 Professional Readiness (AIC1005/AIC1100 + AIC3005). tccns mirrors the local course code (AIC is in Massachusetts; no TCCNS). transfer_confidence is 'core_only'.
